description: Chrome that recedes during consumption and returns on intent. A header states where the user is and offers the way back; it is never louder than the content beneath it.

MUST: Take the page inset as its horizontal padding, so its content starts on the content column rather than at a chrome gutter — a leading title lines up with the body text beneath it.
Resolve its height from the width class.
Render on glass over media, and on a solid surface everywhere else.
Keep its back affordance reachable by pointer and keyboard, not by edge gesture alone.
Pause auto-hide while assistive navigation is active, so controls never vanish under a screen-reader cursor.
Restore itself on intent — a tap, a scroll up, or a focus move into it.
SHOULD: Carry at most one trailing action. A header with three actions is a toolbar wearing a header's clothes.
Truncate its title rather than wrapping, and never truncate data the user must act on.
NEVER: Draw a hairline beneath itself. Separation is the surface step, not a rule.
Place a destructive action in a top corner.
